history.summary: One of the 51 Shakti Peethas. Tradition holds that after Sati immolated herself, Vishnu dismembered her body with his Sudarshan Chakra, and her right ankle (some say anklet/lower limb) fell at this spot on Jhansa Road, Thanesar, known as Devikoop. Legend says the Pandavas with Krishna worshipped Goddess Bhadrakali here before the Mahabharata war, praying for victory, and on succeeding donated their chariot horses - the origin of the age-old tradition of devotees offering silver, mud, or metal horses to the Devi on fulfilment of wishes. The temple's tradition also holds that the tonsure (mundan) ceremony of Krishna and Balaram was performed here. No verified founding date or dynasty is documented.

name: Bhadrakali Shaktipeeth Temple
town_description: Thanesar (ancient Sthanishvara) is the old temple town that grew around the Sthaneshwar Mahadev shrine; it was the capital of the Pushyabhuti dynasty under Emperor Harshavardhana in the early 7th century CE. Today it forms the core of the Kurukshetra urban agglomeration on the Grand Trunk Road in Haryana, anchoring the 48-kos Kurukshetra pilgrimage circuit with Brahma Sarovar, the Shaktipeeth, and the Mahabharata battlefield sites. The town draws pilgrims year-round and is busiest during Gita Jayanti, solar-eclipse fairs, and Maha Shivaratri.

travel.road: On Jhansa Road, opposite Jindal Park, Kuber Colony, Thanesar; well connected by road from Delhi via NH-44

visitor_information.best_time: September-February; Navratri for special decorations and crowds; early mornings best to avoid rush
